key_findings.detail:
Na⁺ ions in the silicon emitter act as compensation centers for the donor species (phosphorus in p-type Si cells). At sufficient concentrations:

- Scanning capacitance microscopy (SCM) shows **carrier concentration changes at the p-n junction** after PID
- Na diffusion onto Si cell surface reduces n-type layer carrier concentration
- A **shallow p-n junction** is observed after PID, compared to a clear depletion region before
- [[papers/Elsevier-541-3483-2-s2.0-84991699729-2016-J-Microscopic aspects of potential induced degradation phenomena and their recovery processes for p ty.pdf#page=5|Luo et al. (2016), p.5]]

Metal ion (Na⁺) accumulation in the depletion region increases recombination current density (J_R), which directly reduces Voc:

- Simulated effect at 300 K with iron-group metal ions:
  - 0 metal ions: minority carrier lifetime τ = 2.18 × 10⁻⁶ s, Voc = 0.640 V
  - 1.0 × 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ ions: τ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ s, Voc = 0.337 V
  - A 218× reduction in lifetime yields ~47% reduction in Voc
- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=4|Wang et al. (2018), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: Dark J-V Signature of Junction Modification
key_findings.detail:
PID-affected modules show characteristic changes in the dark forward J-V curve:

- Increased forward dark current density (steeper rise in dark J-V)
- Module 3 (severe PID, 48.67% power loss): steeper forward current rise than Module 2 (moderate PID, 21.9% loss)
- This signature indicates increased recombination current in the depletion region — a direct indicator of junction degradation
- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=5|Wang et al. (2018), p.5]]

key_findings.claim: Spatial Non-Uniformity: Edge vs. Center Cells
key_findings.detail:
Junction modification is spatially non-uniform, being most severe near module edges (highest electric field):

- **Substring 1 (near frame):** Pmax −59.77%, Voc −38.50%, FF −35.21%
- **Substring 2 (center):** Pmax −21.98%, Voc −8.97%, FF −14.57%
- **Substring 3 (near frame):** Pmax −64.98%, Voc −44.30%, FF −38.03%
- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=6|Wang et al. (2018), p.6]]

In TOPCon cells, PID is classified as **PID-polarization** rather than shunting. Positive charge drift in the SiNx ARC alters the surface potential:

- Low boron doping in the p⁺ emitter (~180 Ω/sq, concentration ~1 × 10¹⁹ cm⁻³) produces a weak surface field
- Charge accumulation in SiNx reduces repulsion of minority carrier electrons from the front surface
- This results in: Isc loss **16.4%**, Voc loss **11.1%**, FF loss **1.3%** under dark 60°C/96 h stress
- [[papers/Wiley-105-888-2-s2.0-85183130481-2024-J-Field-representative evaluation of PID-polarization in TOPCon PV modules by accelerated stress testi.pdf#page=3|Luo et al. (2024), p.3]]

Moderate PID produces reversible junction modification; severe PID leads to permanent changes:

- Moderate PID: near-complete recovery (95.6% Pmax after 487 days natural recovery)
- Severe PID (complete blackout in EL): incomplete recovery (62.8% Pmax after 491 days)
- The irreversible portion corresponds to Na⁺ that has diffused into the bulk p-n junction and cannot out-diffuse thermally at room temperature
- [[papers/Other-81-1747-2-s2.0-85129456088-2022-other-Monitoring the natural recovery of potential induced degradation in poly-crystalline photovoltaic mo.pdf#page=5|Kwembur et al. (2022), p.5]]
